title: Home in Grambling, Louisiana
value: Grambling State University is a historically Black university in Grambling, Louisiana. Its campus address is 403 Main Street, Grambling, LA 71245.

title: A legacy that began in 1901
value: Grambling State University opened on November 1, 1901, as the Colored Industrial and Agricultural School.

title: Our founding president
value: Charles P. Adams was Grambling State University's founding president. Booker T. Washington sent him to help organize the school.

title: Becoming Grambling State
value: The institution adopted the name Grambling State University in 1974.

title: Black & gold, always
value: Grambling State University's school colors are black and gold.

title: Home of the Tigers
value: Grambling State's athletic teams are known as the Tigers and Lady Tigers.

title: Part of the SWAC
value: Grambling State competes in NCAA Division I and the Southwestern Athletic Conference (SWAC).

title: Your space to connect and create
value: Grambling State's library is the Digital Library and Learning Commons, a space for research, studying, and collaboration.

title: More room to learn
value: The Digital Library and Learning Commons offers more than 150 computer stations, 17,000 square feet of study space, and spaces for events and meetings. Check with students for current availability.

title: The legacy of Coach Rob
value: The Eddie G. Robinson Museum is on the Grambling State campus at 126 Jones Street. It honors the legendary Tigers football coach and his legacy.
